title: New-Hire Onboarding
description: The most important things to know in your first week: how Quiz Lab is built and shipped, the dev workflow, the pack schema, and how work flows through Studio AI.

questions.prompt: Where does the live Quiz Lab app run?
choices: On GitHub Pages as a static site
On an AWS server behind an API
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab is served from GitHub Pages under the base path /product-demo — a fully prerendered static site, not Vercel (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: Which framework and adapter is Quiz Lab built with?
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab is a SvelteKit 2 app built with Vite and @sveltejs/adapter-static, so it prerenders to a fully client-side static site (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: Which database stores Quiz Lab's content and leaderboards?
choices: There is no database — all content ships in the build
questions.explanation: There is no server runtime and no database; all quiz content ships inside the static build. Docs that mention Postgres or Vercel are out-of-date marketing, not the live architecture (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: What single action ships a change to production?
choices: Merging a pull request to main
Pushing to a release branch each Friday
questions.explanation: Merging a PR to main is what ships: a GitHub Actions workflow then builds the site and publishes it to Pages. There is no separate deploy step or manual release (Engineering Handbook; Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: Where in the repo do quiz pack JSON files live?
questions.explanation: Packs are one JSON file each in app/src/lib/data/packs/. The old static/quizzes/ location belongs to the deprecated v0 format and must not be used (Pack Authoring Guide; Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: How does a new pack get added to the app?
choices: Drop a JSON file in the packs directory and open a PR
questions.explanation: You add a pack by dropping a JSON file in app/src/lib/data/packs/ and opening a PR — no backend changes or migrations, because there is no backend. It appears on the next merge to main (Architecture Overview; Product Vision & Glossary).

questions.prompt: How many answer choices must each question have?
questions.explanation: Every question's choices array must have exactly 4 options (Pack Authoring Guide). The old v0 format allowed any length, but it is superseded.

questions.prompt: How is the correct answer recorded on a question?
choices: A `correct` string holding the answer text
A `correctIndex` integer from 0 to 3 into choices
A boolean flag on the right choice
It is always the first item in choices
questions.explanation: The current schema uses correctIndex, an integer 0–3 that indexes into choices. Storing the answer as a `correct` string is the deprecated v0 shape and is invalid (Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: What are the valid values for a question's `difficulty` field?
questions.explanation: difficulty is an integer of 1, 2, or 3, rendered as ★ to ★★★. Packs should also mix difficulties rather than make every question level 1 (Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: How many questions should a pack contain?
questions.explanation: The style rules call for 10–15 questions per pack, with mixed difficulty (Pack Authoring Guide).

choices: Factual and grounded in a source document
questions.explanation: Explanations are required, non-empty, and must be factual and grounded in a source — for harder questions you cite the source. Inventing facts is not allowed (Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: In Studio AI, what is an 'idea'?
choices: A hypothesis to validate, broken into PR-sized tasks
questions.explanation: An idea is a hypothesis with a technical design; it is broken into discrete, PR-sized tasks linked to it as ideaSubtasks (Engineering Handbook; Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: What is the branching and merge policy for the repo?
choices: Commit directly to main, revert if broken
Gitflow with a long-lived develop branch
Trunk-based: land work via a reviewed, squash-merged PR; never commit directly to main
Merge a release branch once a quarter
questions.explanation: We practice trunk-based development: main is always releasable, and every change lands through a short-lived branch and a reviewed, squash-merged PR (Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: When an agent picks up a task with work_on_next_task, what does it receive in addition to the task spec?
choices: Nothing — it must search for everything
A list of every document in the knowledge base
questions.explanation: At pickup, Studio AI injects the task's curated context — the small 'neighborhood' of relevant documents attached to the task or inherited from its parent idea — so the agent doesn't have to go discover it (Studio AI SDLC & MCP; Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: Roughly how many documents make up a well-curated context 'neighborhood' for a task?
choices: About 5 — the minimum needed and nothing else
questions.explanation: A good neighborhood is about 5 documents — the smallest set the agent needs and nothing else. Curating it up front is the biggest lever on output quality (Studio AI SDLC & MCP; Engineering Handbook).
